sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression of the moo-tagged construct was studied (L1). No quantitative functional assay (e.g., virus infection) for this specific internal-tag construct is reported in the ledger; NOT MEASURED for function.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly names residue 98 of mouse Mxra8 as the insertion point for the 15-aa moo tag in a full-length surface-displayed construct. Python confirms that human MXRA8 residue 98 = R and residue 99 = V, both within the extracellular domain (landmarks: EC 20–341), 244 residues from the TM boundary — well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. Because the citation is for the mouse ortholog, position_evidence is 'inferred' and cited_tag_residue is set to 98 (the mouse residue carrying the published tag). L1 (PMC7163869): A 15-residue 'moo' sequence was inserted after residue 98 of mouse Mxra8 in a full-length, membrane-anchored construct used to study surface expression. Mouse Mxra8 is a close ortholog of human MXRA8; the insertion site is mapped to human residue 98 by sequence correspondence.

sources.claim: The mouse Mxra8 + moo was generated by inserting residues “GEQRVGEQRLGEQRV” after amino acid residue 98.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by anti-tag antibody staining (L2). CHIKV infection support NOT diminished relative to untagged mouse Mxra8 (L3, Fig S1C).
sites.rationale: The signal peptide of human MXRA8 spans residues 1–19 (landmark-authoritative); the mature extracellular N-terminus begins at residue 20 (V). A tag placed 'downstream of the signal peptide' therefore inserts after residue 19 (A), the sole extracellular N-terminal junction — no other reading is possible. Python confirmed residue_before = A (pos 19) and residue_after = V (pos 20). L3 provides the strongest validation: the N-terminal tag did not diminish CHIKV infection, demonstrating both surface display and preserved receptor function. L2 (PMC7163869): An N-terminal tag placed downstream of the signal peptide was used across Mxra8 orthologs to confirm surface expression by antibody staining. L3 (same paper) reports the functional test specifically on mouse Mxra8 bearing this N-terminal tag.

sources.claim: Of note, the N-terminal tag used to detect the avian constructs did not diminish the ability of mouse Mxra8 to support CHIKV infection ( Fig S1C ).

literature_notes: L4 (hamster MXRA8 C-terminal FLAG) and L5 (human MXRA8 isoform 2 C-terminal FLAG) both describe C-terminal FLAG tags appended to full-length, membrane-anchored constructs. The topology landmarks place the C-terminus (residues 363–442) entirely in the intracellular domain; these tags therefore face the cytoplasm and are recorded in other_positions. L2 and L3 are both from the same paper (PMC7163869) and describe the same N-terminal tag experiment; L3 is cited as the primary supporting clip because it provides the functional result. The 'moo' sequence (GEQRVGEQRLGEQRV) is a tandem repeat of the endogenous GEQRV motif found at human residues 95–99, consistent with the insertion being tolerated at this loop.

literature_other_positions.note: Human MXRA8 isoform 2 C-terminal FLAG tag (L5) and hamster MXRA8 C-terminal FLAG tag (L4) are both appended after the last residue of the ORF; topology landmarks place residues 363–442 in the intracellular domain, so these tags face the cytoplasm and cannot serve as extracellular surface labels.
